description: El Mirage, AZ real estate with Teigh Wade, REALTOR®: compact city near Loop 303 and Grand Avenue, 2000s subdivisions, Luke AFB, Dysart Unified and HOA tips.
summary: El Mirage is a compact incorporated city in Maricopa County on the west bank of the Agua Fria River, bordered by Surprise, Sun City and Luke Air Force Base. It was founded in 1937 and incorporated in 1951. Most homes are 2000s-era subdivisions served by Dysart Unified. Teigh Wade, REALTOR®, works here.

sections.h2: El Mirage in a few lines
sections.html:
El Mirage is small on the map but sits in the middle of everything in the northwest Valley. Surprise wraps around it to the west and north, Sun City and Youngtown lie across the Agua Fria River to the east, and Luke Air Force Base is to the south. The city is roughly 16 to 20 miles northwest of downtown Phoenix, depending on the route.

The community started in the 1930s, when farm workers settled on the west bank of the river. It was founded in 1937 and incorporated as a town in 1951, then voted to become a city in 1983. The historic Agua Fria River Bridge, built in 1895, is one of the oldest structures in the area. In 2017 the city opened a new city hall, along with new police and fire stations.

The original townsite near Grand Avenue has older and smaller homes on varied lot sizes, including some manufactured homes. Most of the rest of El Mirage was built in a short burst during the 2000s, when the city grew rapidly and large tracts of farmland were turned into subdivisions. That gives the city a fairly consistent look: stucco detached homes with tile roofs, two-car garages, block-wall backyards and desert landscaping, in one- and two-story plans.

Subdivision names buyers will see include Rancho Mirage, built around 2000 to 2002, along with Sundial and Arizona Brisas. Because many homes were built by the same handful of builders in the same years, floor plans repeat often, which makes comparing homes easier than in an older city.

Pueblo El Mirage RV and Golf Resort is a 55+ community in El Mirage with manufactured homes, park models and RV sites, along with its own golf course and resort amenities. If you are buying a manufactured home in a community like this, understand whether you will own or lease the land under the home, what the monthly lot or space fees cover, and how the community approves new owners.

• Gateway Park and Bill Gentry Park are the two main city parks, and a YMCA-run recreation center with a swimming pool sits next to Bill Gentry Park.
  • Around the city you will also find a splash pad, a skate facility, ball fields, a dog park, a community garden, a senior center and a library.
  • Founders Day in March is one of the city's annual events.
  • The Sundome Center for the Performing Arts in Sun City West and Lake Pleasant Regional Park to the north are both within a short drive.

sections.h2: Buying in El Mirage: what to check
sections.html:
1. HOA. Most subdivisions built since 2000 have an HOA. Dues vary, so ask what is included and whether there is a separate fee at closing. Homes in the original townsite may have no HOA.
  2. Solar. If the home has panels, ask for the contract. Leased systems require the buyer to qualify with the solar company.
  3. Pool. Get a pool inspection along with your general home inspection.
  4. Aircraft noise. El Mirage borders Luke Air Force Base. Look up the base's noise and accident potential zone maps for any address and visit at different times of day. Arizona sellers near military airports are required to disclose that proximity.
  5. Manufactured homes. Confirm how the home is titled and whether the land is owned or leased, since that affects financing.
  6. Utilities. Confirm the electric and water providers for the address; water may come from the city or another provider depending on location.

Teigh walks through each step with you as part of her buyer representation.

US-60 (Grand Avenue) runs along the northeast side of El Mirage, and Loop 303 is just to the west. The Northern Parkway corridor heads east-west to the south, and Loop 101 is a short drive east across the river. El Mirage Road and Thunderbird Road are among the main local routes.

Dysart Unified School District serves El Mirage and is one of the city's major employers. Dysart schools in the city include El Mirage Elementary and Dysart Middle School, and residents attend Dysart district high schools. Confirm assignments for any address directly with Dysart Unified.

With so many similar floor plans nearby, El Mirage homes are often compared side by side. The details that set one apart are condition, upgrades, a newer roof or AC, owned solar, a pool in good shape and a clean, bright presentation. Buyers also ask about the HOA and, for homes on the south side, about the base.

Teigh helps you decide which repairs and updates are worth making before you list, then gets the home ready with staging help that is included for her listing clients. See the home staging options. Her pricing comes from a comparative market analysis of homes like yours, and she never promises a sale price.

El Mirage sits right next to Surprise, where Teigh lives. She is a REALTOR® with HomeSmart Elite Group, HomeSmart, and she will meet you at your home for a consultation.

faqs.a: El Mirage was founded in 1937 and incorporated as a town on June 25, 1951. Residents voted to become a city in 1983. It is an incorporated city in Maricopa County, on the west bank of the Agua Fria River, bordered by Surprise and Luke Air Force Base.

faqs.q: Which school district serves El Mirage?
faqs.a: Dysart Unified School District serves El Mirage, and the district is one of the city's largest employers. Schools in the city include El Mirage Elementary and Dysart Middle School. Confirm the assigned schools for any specific address with Dysart Unified, since boundaries can change.

faqs.q: Is El Mirage near Luke Air Force Base?
faqs.a: Yes. El Mirage borders Luke Air Force Base. If you are buying, review the base's noise contour and accident potential zone maps for the address, and visit at different times of day. Arizona requires sellers to disclose when a property is near a military airport.

faqs.q: What freeways are close to El Mirage?
faqs.a: US-60 (Grand Avenue) runs along the northeast side of the city, Loop 303 is just west, and Loop 101 is a short drive east. The Northern Parkway corridor connects east-west to the south. Together they provide access to I-10 and I-17.

faqs.q: When were most El Mirage homes built?
faqs.a: Most El Mirage homes were built during the 2000s building boom, when farmland became subdivisions such as Rancho Mirage, Sundial and Arizona Brisas. The original townsite near Grand Avenue has older and smaller homes, including some manufactured homes, so build years vary more there.

faqs.q: Is there a 55+ community in El Mirage?
faqs.a: Yes. Pueblo El Mirage RV and Golf Resort is a 55+ community with manufactured homes, park models, RV sites and a golf course. Before buying there, find out whether you would own or lease the land, what the monthly fees include and how new owners are approved.

faqs.q: Do El Mirage homes have HOAs?
faqs.a: Most subdivisions built since 2000 have an HOA, and some older homes in the original townsite do not. HOA dues and rules differ from one subdivision to the next, so request the documents early. Teigh goes over parking, RV and rental rules with buyers before the inspection period ends.

faqs.q: What parks are in El Mirage?
faqs.a: The two main parks are Gateway Park and Bill Gentry Park, and a YMCA-run recreation center with a pool sits next to Bill Gentry Park. Citywide amenities include a splash pad, skate facility, ball fields, dog park, community garden, senior center and library.
